scope_correction: Evidence-package observability is now separated from execution-transcript coherence. OpenDiscoveryTrace provides useful Git-addressable sample artifacts, but its observed harness can collapse multiple declared actions into one structured step, stores only a truncated raw response, and includes simulated tool semantics; therefore declared workflow text cannot be promoted to executed evidence without action-by-action binding. Audit-Closed AI Scientist provides a strong deterministic public-log decision design, but its observed public result package is aggregate rather than a complete per-trial static log archive, and documented regeneration requires Python/package execution. CaSKG remains a time-scoped README-only negative.
timestamp_qc: Git timestamps remain chronology metadata only unless independently bound to public release/evaluated execution. CaSKG should be rechecked only after a repository/artifact change rather than by repeated unchanged polling.

latest_findings.summary: CaSKG official repository remains at the same README-only main revision; no new replay package landed in the checked surface.
OpenDiscoveryTrace publishes Git-addressable sample scientist-agent traces that can be inspected in scheduled Chat without rerunning models/tools, but this positive scope is sample-level only.

OpenDiscoveryTrace current parser/execution loop can collapse a model response containing several declared actions into one structured/executed action or conclusion, while retaining only a 3000-character raw_response prefix.

OpenDiscoveryTrace tool labels do not by themselves establish evidence semantics: web_search is explicitly simulated, and JSON-wrapped python_exec input can be passed directly to Python and fail syntactically.

OpenDiscoveryTrace aggregate success provenance is heterogeneous: 372 frontier traces are summarized, but success n is only 43/42/42 by model and hard difficulty success is null; do not infer a uniform completed verifier without reconstructing analysis semantics.

Audit-Closed AI Scientist implements deterministic acceptance from a public hash-chained log with committed candidate sets, fail-closed evaluation completeness and replayed decision checks; security tests cover several tamper classes.

Audit-Closed benchmark uses the same synthetic data/candidate set across baseline and audit arms and publishes seed/config/source digests, but the observed public result package is aggregate and documented full reproduction requires Python/package execution.

A Git-object-bound per-trial declarative decision transcript is a promising narrow Chat-native replacement for executable replay when the admission rule is simple arithmetic, but repository-bound identity is not independent-witness nonrepudiation.
